title: Arizona: history overview
d: Arizona: the Grand Canyon State, admitted 1912 (48th); capital Phoenix.
definition: Arizona: the Grand Canyon State, admitted 1912 (48th); capital Phoenix.
description: Arizona — "Grand Canyon State" — entered the Union 1912 (48th). Its capital is Phoenix and its largest city is Phoenix. Ancestral Puebloans; Spanish missions. This database tells the state's story: from its first peoples through statehood to the modern era, plus the famous sons and daughters, the industries, and the facts every resident should know.

title: Statehood
description: Arizona achieved statehood 1912 (48th). The road to statehood ran through territorial government, population thresholds, and a congressional enabling act — the standard American path. Mexican then U.S. territory (1848). Statehood Day is still celebrated, and the admission order gives Arizona its number among the states.

title: The statehood story
d: How Arizona went from territory to state.
definition: How Arizona went from territory to state.
description: The statehood story of Arizona: settlement, territorial organization, the push for admission, and finally the star on the flag. Copper and cattle; Hoover Dam era. Every state's admission reflected the national politics of its era — Arizona's story is no exception, and it explains much about the state's character today.

title: Capital: Phoenix
d: Phoenix is the capital of Arizona.
definition: Phoenix is the capital of Arizona.
description: Phoenix has been the seat of Arizona government, home to the capitol building, the supreme court, and the legislature. Capitals are often not the biggest city — Arizona's largest is Phoenix — chosen instead for geography or politics. Visit the capitol: the building itself tells the state's story in stone.

title: Nickname: Grand Canyon State
d: Arizona is known as "Grand Canyon State."
definition: Arizona is known as "Grand Canyon State."
description: The nickname "Grand Canyon State" captures how Arizona sees itself — and how America sees it. Sun Belt boom; retirement haven. State nicknames come from history, geography, or industry, and they appear on license plates, tourism campaigns, and sports teams. The motto goes deeper: "Ditat Deus (God enriches)."

title: Motto: Ditat Deus (God enriches)
d: The state motto of Arizona is "Ditat Deus (God enriches)."
definition: The state motto of Arizona is "Ditat Deus (God enriches)."
description: The motto "Ditat Deus (God enriches)" is Arizona's official creed, adopted by the legislature and carried on the state seal. Copper star on red-blue rays; Spanish colors. Mottos distill a state's ideals into a phrase — learn it, and you understand what the state aspires to be.
